info.bio:
Genesis es uno de los grupos de rock británicos más famosos. Creado a finales de los sesenta, ha mantenido una trayectoria exitosa hasta la década de los noventa.

Durante Octubre de 2006, el grupo anunció una reunión, que se concretó con una gira en el 2007.

Historia

Inicios: 1967–1969

Originarios de Inglaterra, los adolescentes Peter Gabriel, Mike Rutherford, Anthony Phillips y Tony Banks comenzaron su camino musical en la escuela secundaria Charterhouse Godalming, componiendo sencillos para el joven productor Jonathan King. El nombre del grupo alude al Génesis, primer libro de la Biblia. Sus composiciones de ese breve período fueron lanzadas como su álbum debut From Genesis to Revelation (es decir, "desde el Génesis hasta el Apocalipsis") en 1969. Sin embargo, King no les trae ningún beneficio, por lo cual deciden abandonarlo.

Más tarde conocen a otro productor, Tony Stratton Smith, con el que graban su segundo álbum, Trespass, con John Mayhew a la batería. Una vez terminado el disco, Anthony Phillips decide abandonar el grupo por miedo escénico, que le impedía cumplir con las obligaciones de músico en las giras que realizaban, con él se va John Mayhew.

Época Peter Gabriel: 1970–1975

Para sustituir a Anthony Phillips y John Mayhew ingresan el baterista Phil Collins y el guitarrista Steve Hackett, cuya presencia contribuye a definir el sonido característico del grupo, como se aprecia en el siguiente álbum, Nursery Cryme. Comienza así un período en el que el aspecto teatral de sus actuaciones en vivo (cambios de vestuario, maquillaje y la particular interpretación de Gabriel como vocalista y showman) cobra tanta importancia como el musical, como puede observarse en la puesta en escena de temas tales como "The Musical Box". Las composiciones, especialmente "Supper's Ready" de Foxtrot, con una duración de aproximadamente 26 minutos, tienen la complejidad de las de otras bandas de rock progresivo.

Las letras también se volvieron más serias y los conciertos estaban saturados de efectos de video y sonido. Esta primera etapa se cierra con la edición de un disco en vivo, titulado Genesis Live, donde las tendencias teatrales quedan finalmente documentadas. El álbum Selling England by the Pound, si bien siguió esta misma línea, demostró una maduración extraordinaria de la banda lo que hizo que sea considerado por muchos el disco más representativo del período de Peter Gabriel en Genesis. Selling England by the Pound es el álbum más sofisticado del grupo.

No obstante, esta etapa no duraría mucho. El lanzamiento del ambicioso LP doble llamado The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway a finales de 1974 marcó la última participación de Gabriel en el grupo. En Agosto de 1975, al terminar la gira de presentación de este disco bisagra en la historia del rock mundial, Gabriel anunciaría, por motivos personales, el apartamiento de la conformación.

Época Phil Collins: 1976–1996

Ante rumores de separación definitiva se realizaron audiciones para reemplazar al cantante lo cual parecía una tarea destinada al fracaso. Sin embargo el grupo prefería que Collins tomara el rol de cantante, lo que venía haciendo satisfactoriamente durante algunos ensayos en esos tiempos. La banda regresó a los estudios como un cuarteto en Octubre de 1975 para comenzar su nuevo álbum. El resultado fue A Trick of the Tail, que llegó a ser número tres en Inglaterra y número 31 en Norteamérica (el mejor puesto conseguido por un álbum de Genesis hasta entonces). El éxito confundió completamente a los críticos que no podían concebir a Genesis sin Peter Gabriel. Este disco permite entrever la distinta orientación que la banda adoptaría en lo musical, precisamente más dirigida al éxito en lo comercial que a la revolución musical que de Trespass a The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway había producido. Para las presentaciones en vivo, el grupo contrató a un baterista, ya que Phil Collins debía cantar. Bill Bruford, ex-miembro de Yes y King Crimson, se unió al grupo para una parte de la gira. Después de eso, Chester Thompson tomó la tarea.

La partida de Hackett

Después, el grupo empezó a grabar Wind & Wuthering, en Septiembre de 1976. El disco fue sacado en Estados Unidos a finales de 1976, y en la primera semana de 1977 en el Reino Unido. Estos discos serían presentados durante una gira que concluiría con la edición del disco en vivo Seconds Out que es considerado el cierre definitivo y despedida del Genesis progresivo, debido a que Steve Hackett anunció su partida del grupo durante el tiempo en que se editaba Seconds Out. Seconds Out contiene varias genialidades de la época Peter Gabriel, como el último segmento de "The Musical Box", y versiones íntegras de "Supper's Ready" y "The Cinema Show", entre otras.

Hackett fue reemplazado por Daryl Stuermer para proseguir las giras americanas y europeas, pero no hubo sustituto en el estudio, pues Mike Rutherford podía tocar las parte de bajo y de guitarra. Con esto, el grupo quedó reducido a tres miembros oficiales.

En 1978, un Genesis reducido lanzó And Then There Were Three, con el que el grupo inicia una etapa mucho más comercial y si bien la banda todavia mantuvo al progresivo como estilo para este album, tambien ya se notaba una propuesta mucho mas accesible . De esta época destacan los álbumes Duke, (el cual se convirtió en su primer álbum número uno en Inglaterra mientras ascendía al puesto número 11 en Norteamérica), Genesis ,Abacab (considerado por muchos el peor disco de la banda) e Invisible Touch. De este último trabajo salen "Tonight, Tonight, Tonight", "Invisible Touch", "In Too Deep" y en particular el hit rockero "Land of Confusion", que además fue galardonado por tener uno de los mejores vídeos de ese año.

Ya en los últimos años sale We Can't Dance (1991), que continúa la línea del rock/pop con variados estilos característicos del grupo. Este álbum debutó como número uno en Inglaterra y alcanzó el número cuatro en Norteamérica. "No Son of Mine" y "Jesús He Knows Me" treparon con facilidad a los rankings mundiales, además de "Driving the Last Spike" y "Fading Lights", que mantiene su vieja línea sinfónica/progresiva. Este álbum es el trabajo más vendido de Genesis hasta la fecha.

Época Ray Wilson: 1997–1998

La exitosa carrera como solista de Phil Collins y su vida familiar lo llevó a abandonar el grupo en 1996. Sin embargo, la banda aún logra lanzar en 1997 el disco Calling All Stations con Ray Wilson como cantante principal. El disco se vendió bastante en Europa y el sencillo "Congo" alcanzó la posición 29; pero ni los críticos ni los fans se preocuparon por el disco en Estados Unidos, en donde se vendió poco y no tuvo éxito. La gira en EE.UU. fue cancelada por eso. Tras finalizar la gira europea, los dos miembros originales despiden a Wilson y deciden retirarse temporalmente.

En 1998 se lanza la compilación de cuatro discos Genesis Archive 1967-75 en la que se presenta material inédito junto a grabaciones en vivo con Gabriel como cantante. Después en 1999 salió Turn It on Again: The Hits, una compilación que contenía la mayoría de los grandes éxitos de la era Phil Collins, además de "I Know What I Like", de Selling England by the Pound y una nueva versión de "The Carpet Crawlers" interpretada por la alineación de la época Peter Gabriel, aunque los cinco miembros no estuvieron juntos en el mismo estudio durante la grabación; grabaron sus partes en estudios distintos.

En el 2000 salió otra compilación, esta vez de tres discos: Genesis Archive #2: 1976-1992, que contenía material de la época en la que Phil Collins fue la voz principal.

Turn It on Again: 2006–actualidad

Para el año 2007 se ha anunciado una gira por Europa que los traerá nuevamente por los escenarios, siempre con Phil Collins como voz principal. Por su parte, Peter Gabriel y Steve Hackett no iniciarán el tour con la banda. Gabriel asegura que no excluye la posibilidad de unirse a ellos de nuevo, pero en el futuro, pues actualmente quiere concentrarse en su propio trabajo.

Paralelamente a esta gira se re-editará toda la discografía de Genesis en formato SACD y DVD con audio de alta definición, sonido envolvente y remasterizado.

Durante el mes de junio se inició la gira "Turn It on Again", la cual constó aproximadamente de 20 conciertos en Europa y 20 en Estados Unidos. Dentro de las composiciones, destacó nuevamente la capacidad del grupo para componer "medley", que, en este caso, permitía la unión de los temas "In the Cage" y "Cinema Show", de sus primeros años, junto a "Duke's travels" y "Afterglow", ambos de la segunda mitad de los setenta.

De esta gira se recopiló el disco "Live Over Europe", y  además se ha anunciado un DVD titulado "When in Rome" para el 2008

scenes.name: Rock progresivo
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Al emigrar a Gran Bretaña, el rock se convierte en mercancía de moda pero también se descontextualiza: lo que en EE UU era el diario de la juventud se vuelve en Gran Bretaña un ensayo. El progresivo no comenta la cultura juvenil sino que busca la innovación técnica: arranca con las óperas rock (S.F. Sorrow, Tommy) y los álbumes conceptuales, lo cimentan Traffic, Jeff Beck, Jethro Tull, Family y Genesis, y alcanza su cima con King Crimson (In The Court Of The Crimson King), Van Der Graaf Generator y Yes. Colosseum, la Third Ear Band (inventores de la world music), las variantes góticas (High Tide, Black Widow) y folk (Comus, Strawbs), Gentle Giant, Emerson Lake & Palmer y Roxy Music, que revoluciona el género y prepara la new wave y el synth-pop.

podcast.title: Mid-1975 Evolution
podcast.body: In mid-1975, Genesis began a significant evolution influenced by numerous factors beyond just Peter Gabriel's departure. The music market itself was shifting, and despite progressive rock's popularity (with bands like King Crimson and Pink Floyd filling stadiums), Genesis chose to evolve with these market changes and public taste. "a mitad de 1975, justo a mitad de los 70, se dan muchos factores que hacen que el genesis empieza a dar un cambio a dar una evolución."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: GENESIS con Peter Gabriel VS. Phil Collins

podcast.title: Peter Gabriel Left 1975; Phil Collins Replaced Him After 40 Auditions; Ray Wilson Later Filled In
podcast.body: Peter Gabriel was Genesis's founding singer from 1967 until his departure in 1975, which nearly ended the band. After approximately 40 auditions, they chose their own drummer Phil Collins, whose tenure extended the band's commercial reach considerably. In 1996–2000, when Collins was occupied with his solo career, a singer named Ray Wilson fronted the band before Collins returned. "You know, that worked out okay, didn't it?"

podcast.title: Major Reunion (2011)
podcast.body: Genesis reunited in 2011 for a major tour, an event that serves as a comparison point for the scale and impact of other significant band reunions. "Genesis in 2011..."

podcast.title: 70s Golden Age of Concept Albums
podcast.body: Genesis was a prominent band during the golden age of the concept album in the 1970s. "The golden age of the concept album was in the 1970s. Yes, Rush, Genesis, the All-In-Parsons project, Morph in the Kinks, and of course Pink Floyd."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Adaptation to Market Trends
podcast.body: Genesis successfully evolved with the musical market and its audience, avoiding remaining "anchored" in a progressive rock style that began to go out of fashion. This adaptation, though perhaps not appreciated by all "golden era" fans, allowed the band to remain relevant. "genesis fue una banda que sigo evolucionando con el mercado musical y precisamente con el público musical."

podcast.title: Album Art Designed by Storm Thorgerson
podcast.body: Genesis's album covers were among the many iconic designs created by the renowned Storm Thorgerson and his partner Aubrey Powell. Their collaborations significantly contributed to the visual identity of major progressive rock bands. "That includes Pink Floyd, Black Sabbath, Led Zeppelin, ACDC, the police, Genesis..."

podcast.title: Collective Creative Contribution
podcast.body: Genesis is characterized as a band where all members consistently played an important role in its creative development and success, rather than being dominated by a single visionary leader. "Gensys siempre ha sido una de esas bandas en las que todos los miembros han tenido una parte importante del desarrollo creativo del éxito creativo de la banda. No ha sido de esas bandas que hay un gran líder que es un visionario que lo hace todo."

podcast.title: Contribution to "Monty Python and the Holy Grail"
podcast.body: Genesis, along with Led Zeppelin, provided financial support for the film "Monty Python and the Holy Grail" after Pink Floyd encouraged them to contribute to the project, which was facing funding challenges. "They later got Led Zeppelin and Genesis to kick in a few Bob and the movie was made."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Counter-Movement Inspiration
podcast.body: The "lugubrious, intricate, wady" elements found in the music of Early Genesis, highly prized by progressive rock fans, were precisely the aspects that the emerging back-to-basics rock musicians were attempting to counter in their own artistic efforts. "The very things that progressive rock fans prized in the music of ELP, Yes, Pink Floyd and Early Genesis. These were what the musicians I'm going to focus on today were trying to counteract."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Incredibly Complex Last Stage
podcast.body: Genesis, particularly during Peter Gabriel's final period with the band, produced albums that were considered incredibly complex and passionate. "Algunos discos de genesis de esa última etapa de Peter Gabriel son apasionantes pero son increíblemente complejos."

podcast.title: Peter Gabriel vs. Phil Collins Duality
podcast.body: A long-standing debate revolves around whether Genesis's era with Peter Gabriel or its 1980s era with Phil Collins was superior. The critic argues that this perceived duality is an oversimplification, believing that the band's evolution would have followed a similar path even if Peter Gabriel had remained, driven by broader market changes. "Hay una grandísima dualidad en el mundo sobre que Gensys es mejor, si el Gensys original de Peter Gabriel o Gensys casi de los 80 que tenía Phil Collins."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: GENESIS con Peter Gabriel VS. Phil Collins

podcast.title: Phil Collins as Drumming Hero
podcast.body: Phil Collins, particularly during his time with Genesis, was one of Taylor Hawkins' drumming heroes. Collins' influential style in the progressive rock genre contributed to Hawkins' own musical development. "and Phil Collins when he was with Genesis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-1980s Decline
podcast.body: The band's later stages, particularly after the 1980s, were not as strong. This decline is attributed not to a decrease in musical quality, but to the increasing number of parallel projects undertaken by individual members (such as Phil Collins' solo career and Mike + The Mechanics), which meant Genesis was no longer their primary focus. The band experienced a "slow agony" with music described as increasingly "banal" and "easy," leading to an "unromantic" end. "la última etapa de Jagenesis, bueno ya no fue lo que era."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.body: Genesis sold their catalog of material recorded after Peter Gabriel's departure for $300 million. "Genesis and all their post-Peter Gabriel material, $300 million"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Preference for Peter Gabriel's Mid-Era
podcast.body: The critic personally prefers the albums from *Foxtrot* onwards, up until Peter Gabriel's departure, highlighting these as the band's strongest works from that period. "si me quedo con uno o con otro sinceramente me quedo con los tres últimos discos antes de la marcha de Peter Gabriel del Foxtrot para adelante."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: GENESIS con Peter Gabriel VS. Phil Collins

podcast.title: Reunion Rumors and Future Uncertainty
podcast.body: For 15 to 20 years, there have been rumors of a Genesis reunion, and while some concerts have occurred, a full return is considered increasingly improbable. The current members, including Peter Gabriel and Phil Collins, lack the musical relevance they once had, making a full-scale comeback difficult to close definitively. "llevamos 15 años, 20 años hablando o teniendo rumores sobre la posibilidad de Jagenesis aunque algunos conciertos se han dado pero yo creo que ha diado y yo creo que cada vez está más complicada la vuelta de Jagenesis."

podcast.title: Reunion for Touring
podcast.body: Genesis was one of many bands from past decades that reunited in the 21st century, a trend largely motivated by financial incentives. With declining CD sales impacting artist revenues, returning to the touring circuit offered a lucrative way to appeal to nostalgic fan bases and fill large venues. "The list of reunions is long."

podcast.body: Peter Gabriel notably did not attend Genesis's induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. This absence highlighted the complex, unresolved relationships within the band, as members, despite their past stardom, are no longer active forces in the contemporary music scene. "cuando fueron al jol de la fama Peter Gabriel no fue lo cual ya no se prendió bastante."

xref.title: First Recording at Sun Studios (1953)
xref.body: On July 18, 1953, a young truck driver named Elvis Presley recorded two songs, "That's When Your Heartaches Begin" and "My Happiness," at Sun Studios in Memphis as a birthday present for his mother. These were Elvis Presley's first recordings ever, and based on this session, studio head Sam Phillips helped Elvis become the iconic figure he would be. This record is argued to be the genesis of all rock and roll. Jack White later purchased this one-of-a-kind artifact for $305,000 US, subsequently digitizing and re-releasing it through Third Man Records so the world could hear it. "This is on July 18th, 1953, a young truck driver dropped into Sun Studios in Memphis to record himself singing a song for his mother."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Debut of Ziggy Stardust (July 8, 1972)
xref.body: On July 8, 1972, David Bowie introduced the world to his character Ziggy Stardust at the Royal Festival Hall in London. This marked the genesis of the "world's first synthetic, pre-packaged, ultra-theatrical rock star," lasting 360 days and becoming a highly influential piece of marketing and PR in rock history. "That night, David Bowie stepped on stage at the Royal Festival Hall in London and introduced himself by saying, hi, I'm Ziggy."

xref.title: Debut Performance at CBGB (August 14, 1974)
xref.body: On Wednesday, August 14, 1974, The Ramones played their first-ever show at the iconic New York club CBGB. The initial audience was sparse, consisting of fewer than a dozen people, including the club owner's dog. However, by the end of 1974, the band had performed at CBGB 74 times, with each gig progressively increasing their buzz. The club soon became packed with a diverse crowd, attracting Andy Warhol's circle, intellectuals, wealthy uptown youths seeking to "slum it," and music fans bored with existing sounds and looking for novelty. The Ramones' distinctive style — four "brothers" dressed in torn jeans and leather jackets, playing 1960s-style "bubble gum pop songs" at "a million miles an hour," without solos, stage interaction, or audience acknowledgment, pausing only when Johnny counted off the next song — marked the genesis of the New York punk rock revolution. "The Ramones played their first ever show at a New York club called CBGB."

xref.title: Formation Origin - Pickup Basketball Game (1989)
xref.body: The band's genesis began in Seattle when Stone Gossard and Jeff Ament formed Love Company and sought a singer by circulating a demo. Jack Irons, a former Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer, received a copy of this demo and passed it to Eddie Vedder, a surfer and night shift worker at a Chevron tank farm in San Diego, after a pickup basketball game in 1989. Eddie then wrote lyrics to three of the demo's five songs, dubbed them onto a new cassette, and sent it to Seattle, leading to his invitation to jam with the group and the formation of Pearl Jam. "This cassette passed out of a gym bag sometime in 1989 might have resulted in the most profitable pickup basketball game ever played."

xref.title: Pandrogyny Project – Matching Breast Implants on Valentine's Day 2005 with Life Partner Lady Jaye
xref.body: Genesis P-Orridge, founder of Throbbing Gristle (who coined the term "industrial music" with their 1977 debut *The Second Annual Report*) and later Psychic TV, entered into a relationship with Psychic TV keyboardist Lady Jaye Breyer that was itself conceived as an ongoing performance art piece. The goal was to make the two people look increasingly alike through shared wardrobes, matching haircuts, permanent eyeliner, lip injections, oral surgeries, cheek implants, and ultimately matching breast implants, received together on Valentine's Day 2005. Their shared identity was to be called Ms. Breyer P-Orridge — a merged being making a statement about the oneness of humanity and the obsolescence of traditional gender roles. Genesis retained his original genitalia; Lady Jaye declined to have anything added. Lady Jaye died on October 9, 2007, from a previously undiagnosed heart condition possibly connected to her long-term battle with stomach cancer. "Their goal was to merge their identities into a single being."

xref.title: Brandon Flowers' Personal Inspiration
xref.body: The genesis of "Mr. Brightside" came from a deeply personal experience for singer Brandon Flowers. As a 19-year-old, he was living in Las Vegas with his sister, renting a room for $200 a month, and was heartbroken after walking into The Crown and Anchor bar and seeing his ex-girlfriend, his first serious relationship, with another man. This betrayal inspired the song's narrative. "Somewhere at the root of all this, at all these achievements and profits is a real woman."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Chanie Wenjack Story as Genesis
xref.body: The story of Chanie Wenjack, who died trying to walk home from a residential school, was recounted to Gord by his brother Mike after Mike read it in McLean's magazine. This story became the foundational inspiration for Gord's "Secret Path" project. "Mike Downey, Gord's brother, ran across the story in McLean's magazine and told Gord all about it. And that was the genesis of everything."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Contribution to "Monty Python and the Holy Grail"
xref.body: Led Zeppelin, alongside Genesis, was encouraged by Pink Floyd to financially contribute to the production of the film "Monty Python and the Holy Grail," which was struggling to secure funding. "They later got Led Zeppelin and Genesis to kick in a few Bob and the movie was made."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Drumming Influences
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins' drumming style was heavily influenced by progressive rock drummers such as Neil Peart of Rush, Stewart Copeland of The Police, and Phil Collins during his time with Genesis. Other influences included Stephen Perkins of Jane's Addiction, Ringo Starr, and his hero, Roger Taylor of Queen. "His heroes were Neil Pirate of Rush, Stuart Copeland of the police, and Phil Collins when he was with Genesis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation at University of Massachusetts
xref.body: The band the Pixies originated at the University of Massachusetts, marking an academic genesis that subtly aligns with the intellectual curiosity often associated with nerd culture. "First of all, the band was born at the University of Massachusetts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Funding for "Monty Python and the Holy Grail"
xref.body: The significant earnings from Pink Floyd's "Dark Side of the Moon" album provided crucial financial support for the production of the film "Monty Python and the Holy Grail." The band members, who enjoyed watching Monty Python on the BBC during recording breaks, donated £200,000 to the Pythons after learning of their funding difficulties, and also encouraged Led Zeppelin and Genesis to contribute. "When they were working on the record, the band would relax by watching Monty Python on the BBC. When they heard that the pythons were struggling to make the movie, they sent Python a check for two hundred thousand pounds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Glam Rock Genesis
xref.body: David Bowie was significantly inspired by Mark Bolan, a former folk musician who formed the psych band T-Rex. Bolan's appearance on "Top of the Pops" in March 1971, wearing satin clothes covered with glitter dust, struck Bowie as brilliant and marked the beginning of Glam Rock. "This was the beginning of Glam Rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Haircut as Catalyst for Musical Change
xref.body: It is posited that David Bowie's immense impact on music, which fundamentally reshaped its future, might have had its genesis in the seemingly simple act of getting a new haircut. "And to think that it might have all started with a haircut."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Highest-Grossing Reunion Tour of All Time (Projected)
xref.body: The Oasis reunion tour is projected to become the highest-grossing reunion tour in history, surpassing previous records set by bands such as The Police, Led Zeppelin, The E Street Band, Genesis, and Black Sabbath. "I don't know, whatever you want to compare it to, this will be the highest grossing reunion tour of all time."

xref.title: Kingston Origins and Early Formation
xref.body: The core members originated from Kingston, where they were part of a vibrant music scene that also produced The Tragically Hip. The band's genesis involved a group called "Sean Penn Atenshry" in the mid-1980s, which included Hugh Dillon, Randy Kwan, Mark Gibson, and Frontini, before Trent Carr joined and transformed their sound, leading to The Headstones' formation. "So how the headstones come out of Kingston? What year are we talking about? 89? No, you came from Kingston earlier than that. It was like 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Headstones: In Their Own Words Part 1

xref.title: Ongoing Mobility Issues
xref.body: Phil Collins's health challenges have continued for years, requiring treatment in a hyperbaric chamber for an infected diabetic abscess on his foot. He frequently relies on a cane for support and occasionally uses a wheelchair due to persistent problems with his back and hips. During the very last Genesis tour, he performed all his sets sitting down, with his son Nic taking over drumming duties. "He needs a cane and sometimes resorts to a wheelchair because of continuing problems with his back and hips."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Origin of Ambient Music (Car Accident)
xref.body: The genesis of ambient music for Brian Eno came after a 1975 car accident left him bedridden for several months. Unable to adjust the volume of very quiet "heart music" playing, he experienced an epiphany, realizing that music could possess properties similar to color or light in creating a harmonious and balanced sensory experience. "In 1975, he got into a car accident, and this led him bedridden for several months."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
